title: Extract the Orchestrator into orchestrator-os behind one host seam; Agent OS selects the engine through one bridge
summary: The Orchestrator moves to the orchestrator_os package (repository unwit1/orchestrator-os) by mechanical copy from personal-agent-os@ce09ad2 with a file-level provenance map, not a history rewrite. orchestrator_os.host is the only stand-in for Agent OS: state root (ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_ROOT, editable checkout, ~/.orchestrator-os; legacy layout detected), machine config dir, and optional project services served by StandaloneHost or agent_os.orchestrator_host. Agent OS picks internal or external engine with AGENT_OS_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND (default internal until cutover). Orchestrator-owned evidence (evals, records, provider policy, prior art, improvement backlog) moves to state/; checkpoints and status remain Agent OS session history. Harness2 is adopted only as an optional offline lab through its BenchmarkAdapter/Proposer seams (Option C); its executors are never used. Extraction exposed three control-plane path assumptions, fixed with tests.

prior_art.checked: Ingester Engine extraction (ingester_bridge.py) as in-house precedent; google-research/harness2 implementation review; git subtree/filter-repo for history
prior_art.found: ingester_bridge resolves an installed package or sibling checkout; Harness2 exposes BenchmarkAdapter (12 methods) and an overridable Proposer.call
prior_art.reused: the bridge pattern (one resolver, explicit install hint); Harness2 deterministic demo as the first pipeline check
prior_art.why_custom: the host seam is ~200 lines of forwarding over existing functions; no library offers it
